newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris urges mutineers in Bangui to lay down arms.
newsitem.headline: Paris urges mutineers in Bangui to lay down arms.

text.p: Paris urged mutineers and private militia in the Central African Republic on Wednesday to give up their arms, warning that failure to do so could plunge the nation into new fighting.
"France urges all concerned parties to begin turning in their arms, without which the country could fall into chaos," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
It said the mutineers had agreed to turn in their weapons as part of a January agreement to restore peace to the capital Bangui after three army revolts in less than a year.
The French ministry said that a relative calm prevailed in Bangui after five days of clashes in which at least 58 people have died.

But witnesses said that over 300 marchers supporting the mutineers had marched through the capital's streets earlier in the day in protest against French support for African peacekeepers trying to crush them.
The demonstrators, who marched peacefully to the French embassy, accused the former colonial power and the peacekeepers of siding with President Ange-Felix Patasse in the civil conflict.
Rummelhardt said that 28 French nationals including numerous children had been flown out of Bangui on Tuesday in a military aircraft.
It said a military plane was used to fly them to the Gabon capital Libreville after state-owned national airline Air France cancelled its scheduled Tuesday flight to Bangui.
"The French community is remaining calm under difficult circumstances," Rummelhardt said.

The peace deal the African force came to implement was preceded by three mutinies within a year, in which political and ethnic supporters of Patasse in the army clashed with former comrades who became bitter enemies.

French troops are stationed in Bangui under a defence accord. Paris, which last year intervened to stop clashes, denied on Tuesday it was directly helping the African force, though it acknowledged it was acting in self-defence.
